If you're running late, you'll probably want to send a text message to the person you're meeting saying that you're running late, and what time you actually expect to get there. I've found that if you say an even later time than the actual time you're expecting to arrive, it usually works out much better. This is because:

  • If you misjudged how long it was going to take to get there the first time, then there's a good chance it'll happen again. Having to send a second message to say you're going to be even later than the first 'late time' you sent does not feel good.

  • You'll arrive feeling more relaxed, knowing that you don't have to rush to meet the time you said in your message, so you'll be in a slightly better mood when you do get there

  • If you do in fact make it for the time you first thought you might get there by, then it looks a bit like you showed up 'early', cause you weren't as late as you said you'd be.
LPT: If you're running late, send a message saying you'll be there at a time *after* the time you expect you'll get there.

And to expand on this idea, when someone asks how long something will take, say it will take significantly longer than it actually will.

Nobody is happy when you say 5 minutes and then take 10. But if you say it'll be a half hour, you can then take 10 minutes to do a 5 minute task, and look like a superstar.

I learned that lesson as a child from Scotty on startrek.
